CITI
Jersey City, NJ
As Senior Vice President, Quality Engineering Manager for Payments Technology, you will own the test strategy for CitiDirect, Citi's award winning digital banking platform that gives clients one-click access to global transaction capabilities across payments, liquidity and trade. You will direct multiple testing teams, set the standards for test automation and User Acceptance Testing, and make sure every release of CitiDirect and its connected systems meets a high quality bar before reaching production. This is an opportunity to shape how a global bank validates mission critical payments technology and to build a modern, automated testing organization.
Responsibilities
Lead the test strategy for CitiDirect and its upstream and downstream applications across the Payments, Liquidity and Trade domains.
Direct multiple testing teams, setting priorities and resolving complex issues that carry significant business impact.
Design and implement User Acceptance Testing scripts and plans together with technology project managers, UAT professionals and business users.
Build testing standards and quality benchmarks that keep automation, documentation and release processes consistent across teams.
Plan and coordinate cross-team testing dependencies to keep releases on schedule and reduce production risk.
Partner with development teams, IT project managers, business stakeholders and external vendors to align testing approach with delivery goals.
Manage team performance and development, including hiring, coaching, compensation decisions and career planning for testing professionals.
Assess risk in every release decision and escalate control issues early to protect Citi and its clients.
Required Qualifications & Skills
10+ years of experience in a testing environment, including senior level people management experience.
Deep understanding of Systems Development Life Cycle processes and end to end testing methodologies.
Hands-on experience with test management tools such as Quality Center and related testing platforms.
Clear and concise written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to negotiate and influence at a senior level.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work through complex and unfamiliar testing situations.
A track record of leading teams to deliver high quality results under tight deadlines.
A bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in a related field.
Beneficial Skills & Qualifications
Working knowledge of API testing tools such as Postman, Rest Assured or SoapUI.
Programming skills in Java, Python or JavaScript, combined with background in payments technology, cloud platforms and Agile or Scrum delivery, and a track record of moving manual QA functions to automated testing.:
Playwright & TypeScript/JavaScript Mastery (Required): Extensive hands-on experience designing and implementing scalable, maintainable test automation frameworks from scratch using Playwright and TypeScript/JavaScript.
CI/CD Pipeline Integration & Quality Gating (Required): In-depth experience establishing continuous testing workflows within CI/CD pipelines, including setting up automated regression triggering and pipeline hard gating.
Containerization & Scaled Infrastructure (Strongly Preferred): Strong background in leveraging Docker and Kubernetes to containerize test suites and horizontally scale distributed test execution across enterprise environments.
GenAI & Agentic Testing Workflows (Strongly Preferred): Experience using AI Harnesses (e.g., GitHub Copilot or Claude) and creating custom AI agents or automated agentic workflows to optimize the software testing lifecycle.
Education:
Bachelor’s/University degree, Master’s degree preferred
What We Offer
Based at Citi's Jersey City location, you will lead a testing function that supports a payments platform used by clients around the world, with the backing and resources of a global technology organization.
Work in a hybrid arrangement with 3 days in the office and 2 days working remotely each week.
Shape testing strategy and standards for a platform operating across global markets, with real influence on outcomes.
Access ongoing learning and leadership development programs to continue growing your career in technology.
Collaborate with testing, development and business teams across multiple geographies and time zones.
Benefit from financial wellbeing programs, healthcare coverage and family support resources.
Apply now to lead the quality engineering strategy behind one of Citi's most critical payments platforms.

Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
Genesis
San Carlos , California 
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.
This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.
What you'll do
Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.
What we're looking for
You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.
Working conditions
Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.
Why this role
You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.
How we work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition.
We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency.
Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun.
Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency.
Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism.
We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego.
Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey.
We take pride in the craft.

Los Angeles, CA
Producers at Riot lead passionate cross-functional teams to craft creative content and incredible experiences for our players. As a Sr. Manager, Game Production

About Doorvest
Doorvest is a venture-backed, long-term-rental property management company. We acquire small property management businesses and integrate them onto one platform, one operating model and one team. Today we manage roughly 2,300 homes across Ohio (Cleveland and Dayton), Texas, Georgia, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Oregon and Florida, built through five acquisitions in under two years, with more under letter of intent. We expect to pass 3,000 doors by year-end and to roughly triple from there in 2027.
We run the business as a multi-site company, not a San Francisco startup with field offices. Our central back office (resident services, collections, evictions, housing programs and compliance, owner success, ops finance) is specialized and partly offshore; our markets are run by General Managers with in-house technicians, local vendors and leasing agents on the ground. We run on Rentvine, Nutiliti, Second Nature and RentEngine, and we build a lot of our own tooling with AI rather than waiting on an engineering sprint.
The role
We are hiring a VP of Operations to own field operations: every market's P&L, maintenance and turns, and the General Managers and maintenance leadership who run them. You will inherit a working structure, not a blank page. Our Senior Maintenance Manager runs company-wide maintenance process, personnel and revenue today and will report to you on day one. Our General Managers (Cleveland, Florida, Oregon) and our Dayton Market Lead report to him today and move to you after a 60-day ramp. In-house technician crews already exist in Cleveland and Oregon, with offshore maintenance coordinators dispatching in every market.
Your job is to make that structure perform and then make it repeatable: turn maintenance into a profit center run in-house wherever the numbers support it, get every market to the same turn times and work-order SLAs, and build the playbook that lets us add the next acquisition's doors without adding chaos. Central Operations owns the phone, the tenant and the owner relationship; you own the truck, the key and the market. The work order is the hand-off between the two, and you will be measured on how fast and how cleanly your side of it closes.
This is a leadership seat with an operator's workload. You will manage managers, but you will also be in the dispatch queue, on a job site and in a vendor negotiation when the week requires it. If you have spent the last several years exclusively managing managers, this will be uncomfortable.
What you will own
Market P&L across every market.
Revenue, margin and cost for field operations and maintenance, market by market, with the General Managers accountable to you for their numbers and you accountable to the COO for the total.
Maintenance as a business.
Pricing, scope capture, billable-hour capture on every work order, the margin between in-house or vendor cost and billed work, estimate review, and the work-order-to-accounts-payable hand-off (billable backfill, invoice coding, owner/tenant/company cost split). The company measures leakage weekly; you own closing it.
Turns and work-order SLAs.
Dispatch, in-house technicians, vendor scheduling, turns, rent-ready and move-in readiness in every market. Resident Services creates the move-out inspection and turn work orders and decides security-deposit charges; your teams complete the inspection with photos, findings and estimates back on the work order within three business days of move-out, then complete the turn.
The field leadership team.
Manage the Senior Maintenance Manager from day one and the General Managers and Market Lead after the ramp. Set each market's scorecard (turn days, work-order SLA, occupancy, escalation SLA, statement exceptions cleared before owner-statement close) and run the weekly business review against it. Hire the next General Managers as we open markets.
Local vendor networks and local hiring.
Source, price, onboard and performance-manage vendors and contractors in every market; decide where in-house crews beat vendors and build them; approve maintenance spend per the authority matrix you will help write.
Inspections, violations and physical loss.
City, Section 8 and lead-safe inspections that Central Operations schedules and your market teams attend; violation cure; property insurance claims coordination for fire, water, mold and displacement, with Owner Success handling the owner.
Business continuity and after-hours.
Incident response for storms, fires and outages; the maintenance on-call layer behind the central after-hours line.
Acquisition integration, field side.
Product owns the integration plan; you own the maintenance and field migration inside it: vendor account transfers, technician onboarding, work-order and SLA standards live in the new market from day 0 to day 90.
Tooling and data.
Build the dispatch views, vendor scorecards, leakage and margin dashboards you need with AI tools, then partner with Product and Engineering to productionize what proves out. Our current dashboards are slow and incomplete; you will help rebuild them.
Playbooks and training.
Document the field SOPs (dispatch, turns, inspections, vendor onboarding, in-house crew standards) into the company knowledge base and run the training that makes a new General Manager productive in 60 days.
How we will measure you
Turn days and work-order SLA attainment by market
Maintenance revenue and margin; billable hours captured on every work order
Move-out inspection work orders closed within three business days: 100%
Leakage dollars (unbilled work, miscoded invoices) trending to zero
Occupancy and in-market escalation SLA per General Manager scorecard
Time from acquisition close to field operations on standard

5+ years managing people, including managing managers, and managing a mixed workforce of in-house crews and external vendors to hard SLAs.
You have carried a P&L or a margin target and can say concretely how you moved it. You have built or grown a maintenance, service or field operation as a revenue line, not only a cost center.
A player-coach who has led a team while still doing work of their own, and who is energized by that rather than insulted by it.

It is not an office job: Cleveland and Austin are where you will be based, and our markets are where the work is. We are looking for an operator who has run a distributed, physical operation, wants to own it as a business, and wants to build the next version of it with real technology and data behind them.
